title: Staff Software Engineer, AI-Native Systems
description:
Staff Software Engineer, AI-Native Systems 

Location: Remote (US)

We are 

Virtual care only works if the infrastructure behind it does. Wheel builds that infrastructure: the systems that let telehealth run at scale for the patients, clinicians, and companies that depend on it. We're not bolting AI onto old workflows; we're rebuilding how care gets delivered, with AI in the product and in how we build it.

We do this in a live, regulated healthcare environment where getting it right matters. This is the next architecture of virtual care, and we're building it now.

You are 

A staff-level engineer who has built software in a regulated, high-stakes domain (ideally health tech; fintech and insurtech count too) and knows what that demands: sensitive data, regulatory constraints, and the cost of getting it wrong. You've designed and shipped AI and agentic systems in production, you know where they break, and you have opinions, held loosely and argued well, about building them safely.

You're a builder first, and you've done real work in small, scrappy teams. You still write the hard parts of the code yourself, and you've done it recently. You don't need a platform org, TPMs, or layers of review to move.

You operate as a domain owner, not a task owner. You take a problem that isn't well-formed, define it, tie it to what the business has committed to, and lead a group of engineers to a shipped, measured outcome. Your impact shows up in other people's work: the patterns they reuse and the ambiguity you removed before it cost the team a quarter.

You get things done. You have sharp judgment about what actually moves the outcome, you'd rather ship something useful this week than something perfect next quarter, and you know when good enough is good enough (and when, in healthcare, it isn't).

And you're good to work with. You're curious, generous with your time, quick to give credit, and you can disagree hard without making it personal. Smart matters here; kind matters just as much. Bonus points if people genuinely enjoy being on a team with you.

The Work 

Technical Leadership & Direction 

- 
Own the technical direction for a significant AI-native area of the platform, such as patient and clinician experiences, care delivery, or the AI platform layer other teams build on.

- 
Act as tech lead for a team or cross-team initiative: break down ambiguous problems, sequence delivery, clear blockers, and keep the team pointed at the outcome rather than the ticket.

- 
Connect day-to-day engineering to quarterly commitments and company goals, and make those links visible to the team.

- 
Write and review design docs. Make and document the load-bearing calls, including "not yet" and "buy, don't build."

AI & Agent Engineering 

- 
Design and build production AI features and agents: retrieval, orchestration, tool calling, guardrails, evaluation, and observability.

- 
Define what "production-ready" means for AI here (testability, rollback safety, cost ceilings, failure modes, human-in-the-loop boundaries) and hold the bar in review.

- 
Take on the hardest parts of the build yourself. This is a hands-on role; you are expected to be in the code every day.

Healthcare-Grade Engineering 

- 
Treat privacy, security, and responsible AI use on sensitive health data as hard engineering requirements, and turn compliance constraints into concrete architecture.

- 
Partner with clinical, compliance, and legal stakeholders early, so safety and review are designed in rather than bolted on.

- 
Build for the realities of healthcare: integrations with clinical systems, auditability, and high-reliability workflows.

Cloud-Native Delivery 

- 
Own full-stack delivery in TypeScript/Node.js and Python: services, APIs, data jobs, and the interfaces on top.

- 
Own deployment, monitoring, and troubleshooting in production, including on-call, and improve the operational posture of what you inherit.

Measure & Improve 

- 
Own the evaluation strategy for your area: metrics, test harnesses, and plans for accuracy, latency, safety, and cost.

- 
Instrument systems so their behavior is legible after the fact, not just at demo time.

- 
Kill approaches that aren't working, early and visibly.

Stakeholders & The Org 

- 
Work directly with product, operations, clinical, and business leaders to decide which use cases are worth building.

- 
Explain trade-offs and risks clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, up to the executive team.

- 
Mentor engineers through code review, design review, and pairing, and build reusable patterns that raise the bar beyond your own team.

What success looks like 

- 
First 30 days: you've shipped something to production, met the people you'll build with, and know where the sharp edges are.

- 
First 90 days: you own an area, set its technical direction, and have shipped AI features with an evaluation story behind them.

- 
First 6 months: patterns you established are used by teams you don't sit on, the business can point to outcomes you drove, and engineers say their work got better (and more fun) because you're here.

What we're looking for 

- 
8+ years building and operating production software, with full-stack depth in TypeScript/Node.js and at least one other language (Python strongly preferred).

- 
3+ years building software in health tech, fintech, or insurtech, including work with sensitive data under HIPAA, PCI, SOC 2, or similar requirements.

- 
Hands-on experience designing and shipping AI or agentic systems in production (retrieval, orchestration, tool calling, evaluation), with a clear view of where LLMs work and where they don't.

- 
A record of shipping outcomes, not just output: you can point to what you delivered, why it mattered, and the judgment calls you made to get it out the door.

- 
Recent hands-on output: in the last two years you've personally built and debugged significant production systems, not only directed others.

- 
Meaningful time at a startup or growth-stage company where you owned what platform, release, or infrastructure teams would handle elsewhere.

- 
A track record of technical leadership as an IC: owning a domain, leading multi-engineer efforts to completion, and driving decisions across teams without positional authority.

- 
A collaborative, low-ego style: you raise the people around you and make hard conversations easier, not harder.

- 
Fluent use of AI development tools as a force multiplier, with judgment about when to trust, verify, or override them.

- 
Strong cloud-native fundamentals: CI/CD, observability, and running what you build. Fluency with relational data and SQL.

- 
Clear written and verbal communication, including design docs that change minds. This is a remote, cross-functional role.

Strongly desired 

- 
Health tech experience specifically: telehealth, EHR/EMR, digital health, payer/provider, or pharmacy.

- 
Experience with clinical workflows or integrations with clinical systems (EHRs, e-prescribing, labs, HL7/FHIR).

- 
Model evaluation and guardrail infrastructure: measuring output quality, catching regressions, and keeping AI inside safe bounds.

- 
Patient-, clinician-, or customer-facing AI products shipped to real users.

- 
Experience building platform capabilities consumed by other engineering teams.

- 
Experience as a formal tech lead or mentoring engineers.

What's hard about this role 

We'd rather you hear it now: 

- 
Ambiguity is the job. Problems often arrive half-formed, and priorities can shift as the business and market change.

- 
You'll build, not just direct. There's no large platform org; you'll write code, run what you ship, and take on-call.

- 
Healthcare raises the bar. Clinical safety, privacy, and compliance review are part of shipping, and they take real time.

If that sounds energizing rather than draining, we'd love to talk.

How we work 

Remote-first (US), fast-moving, with tight loops between engineering, product, clinical, and the business. We're an AI-forward engineering org: we expect AI in the toolchain and in the product, and we measure outcomes over activity. We handle sensitive healthcare data under strict controls; privacy, security, and responsible AI are engineering requirements, not afterthoughts.

We take the work seriously, not ourselves. We're direct and kind, we help each other out, and we have fun doing it.

Salary and Perks 

Pay Range: $185,725-$264,500 USD

Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including, but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the role, the selected candidate’s work experience, education and training, the work location as well as market and business considerations. 

As an employee of Wheel, you’ll enjoy our Total Rewards Program to help secure your financial future and preserve your health and well-being, including:

- 
Medical, Dental and Vision

- 
Ancillary: Life, Short and Long Term Disability

- 
401K match

- 
Flexible PTO

- 
Parental Leave

- 
Stock options

- 
Additional programs and perks

Wheel is committed to equal employment opportunities for all team members. Every decision we make regarding employment is solely based on merit, competence, and performance. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. 

Research shows that underrepresented groups typically apply only if they meet 100% of the criteria listed. At Wheel, we encourage women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ job seekers to apply for positions even if they don’t check every box for the role.

title: Android Software Engineer
description:
About BJAK 

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role 

We are looking for Android engineers to build the native Android experience for BJAK's Android Software Engineer.

This role is for someone who cares about clean user flows, fast performance, product quality and shipping reliable mobile features used by real customers.

What You'll Own 

- 
Build and ship Android features using Kotlin.

- 
Create clean mobile flows for insurance, payments, claims, renewals and financial services.

- 
Work with product and design to simplify complex user journeys.

- 
Integrate backend APIs and ensure mobile flows are stable, secure and reliable.

- 
Improve app performance, crash rate, loading states, responsiveness and memory usage.

- 
Use analytics, user behaviour and production issues to improve the product.

- 
Build AI-assisted mobile experiences only where they genuinely improve the user journey.

What We're Looking For 

- 
3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

- 
Strong Android fundamentals and experience shipping production apps.

- 
Good knowledge of Jetpack, Coroutines, Flow and modern Android architecture.

- 
Strong sense of mobile UX, usability, edge cases and user flows.

- 
Experience integrating REST APIs and debugging production issues.

- 
Fast execution, high ownership and strong attention to product quality.

- 
App links, GitHub, screenshots or examples of shipped work are a strong advantage.

Tech Stack 

- 
Kotlin

- 
Jetpack Compose

- 
Android SDK

- 
Coroutines & Flow

- 
SQL / NoSQL

- 
TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

The Kind of Builder We Want 

- 
Thinks in user journeys, not just screens.

- 
Cares about making complex financial products feel simple.

- 
Moves fast without creating messy code.

- 
Notices UX, performance and reliability issues before users complain.

- 
Honest about what they personally built, what was team-owned and what impact they can or cannot claim.

This Role Is Not For 

- 
Engineers who only want fully defined tickets.

- 
Developers who build screens without caring about user experience.

- 
People who ignore crashes, edge cases, loading states or performance.

- 
Engineers who move slowly in a startup environment.

- 
People who exaggerate impact without explaining their actual contribution.

Location 

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Germany . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Germany .

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process 

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Backend Software Engineer - Indexing
description:
About us: 

DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry.

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage.

Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it.

About the Role:
We’re looking for a Backend Software Engineer to join our team and take meaningful ownership from day one. You’ll work closely with smart, driven, and genuinely fun people who are passionate about tackling the complex challenges involved in building a high-performance product at scale.

Our indexing system is the backbone of our search engine, processing queries over hundreds of millions of documents in fractions of a second. Building and maintaining these indices within tight time and resource constraints requires highly performant, scalable software. To achieve this, we rely on modern technologies in distributed and parallel computing, database systems, and cloud platforms. You’ll leverage the strengths of these technologies to meet demanding throughput and latency requirements.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Design, develop, and maintain efficient, scalable backend services using modern tools and frameworks

- Take ownership of core components of our indexing infrastructure

- Collaborate with other engineers to define, design, and ship new features

- Optimize performance and scalability across our data processing pipelines

- Integrate with third-party data providers and effectively use their APIs

- Review code and contribute to a high standard of code quality and maintainability

- Participate in agile development processes, including sprint planning, daily stand-ups, and retrospectives

You're a great fit if you: 

- Have a Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

- Have 2+ years of experience as a Backend Software Engineer, ideally in a scale-up or fast-growing environment

- Have strong experience with concurrent and parallel programming and understand how to write correct, efficient code under load

- Are highly proficient in Python, our primary backend language. Solid experience with Rust or Go is also very welcome, even if Python isn't your strongest language yet

- Have solid experience working with databases (SQL and/or NoSQL)

- Are comfortable with modern web architectures and cloud platforms

- Enjoy solving complex problems and thinking about performance at scale

- Communicate clearly and enjoy working in a collaborative team

- Take ownership and can work independently when needed

- Have experience with information retrieval or search systems (nice to have)

What you can look forward to: 

- Location: Office 5min walking distance from Zurich central station, where we primarily work on site

- Collaborative and supportive work environment

- Potential for professional growth and advancement within the company

- Ownership and ability to impact the company, product, and culture

At DeepJudge, we believe great teams are built on diverse perspectives and experiences. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If this role excites you, but you feel you don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway and tell us why you’d be a great fit.

location: Denmark,  France,  Netherlands,  Poland,  UK,  USA
description:
About ElevenLabs 

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- 
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- 
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- 
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- 
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- 
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- 
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- 
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- 
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- 
Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- 
Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- 
Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

- 
Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role 

ElevenMusic is a consumer music app where music is the core product: a place to listen, create, remix and stream. The team works in its own environment, separate from the main org, and is agent-first with fast CI, so ideas reach users within a day or two.

You’ll own features end to end, from spotting the problem to shipping the product and the backend behind it. Most of what you build is new, in a space where few companies are working with AI and music, so there’s no playbook. You’ll define the problem yourself, test ideas with real users, and work alongside research engineering to turn model capabilities into things people love using. What you ship goes live to a large audience within days.

You’re a builder with strong product taste who understands every layer of the system. You use AI to move fast, but you own and understand everything you ship. You care about music and the people who make it.

Requirements 

- 
Have shipped and owned a well-designed consumer product from zero to real users, across frontend and backend

- 
Understand your systems deeply enough to spot immediately when a PR is wrong, insecure or needlessly complex

- 
Show excellent product judgement: you know the most valuable thing to build, and what not to build

- 
Work autonomously with minimal direction, and take responsibility for fixing problems as you find them

- 
Have a real interest in music, or in the people who make it

Bonus: Open-source or GitHub track record, experience building music or audio products, or experience with recommendation systems or embeddings.

Location 

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe and the US East Coast, with the ability to operate in GMT-5 to GMT+1 timezones required. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London, New York, Dublin, Amsterdam, and Warsaw.

title: Principal Software Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
The role 

Reporting directly to the VP Technology, you'll build new capability for Awin with AI at the core, free from the constraints of our established delivery model. You'll take ideas from concept to production quickly, prove what works, and turn the best of it into patterns the wider engineering organisation can adopt.

You'll work closely with product and commercial leaders to find where AI changes the economics of our affiliate marketing platform: what we can build, how fast, and at what cost. You'll be hands-on most of the time, writing code, shipping and measuring results, rather than coordinating others.

You'll know enough of our existing platform to connect new things to it safely, but you won't be absorbed into running it. Your job is to show what modern, AI-native engineering looks like at Awin, and make it real.

This is a step-up opportunity. We're looking for a bright, self-starting engineer who is ready for more scope than their current role allows. You might not have held a principal title yet. What matters is that you're already building this way, you learn fast, and you want the room to prove it. You'll have direct access to senior leadership, real problems with commercial weight, and the freedom to choose how you solve them.

Key tasks and accountabilities 

Build and ship 

- Design, build and run AI-powered products, tools and services from prototype to production

- Own outcomes end to end: problem framing, architecture, implementation, evaluation, release and operation

- Run fast, time-boxed experiments; scale what works and stop what doesn't, with the evidence to back either call

- Set up and evolve the AI infrastructure these builds rely on: model access, evaluation tooling, observability and guardrails

Shape direction 

- Work with the VP Technology to set Awin's engineering-specific AI direction, grounded in what has actually been built and measured

- Scope strategic opportunities early with product and commercial leaders, with effort, cost and value made explicit

- Make clear recommendations on build vs buy, model and vendor choice, and where AI should not be used

Architecture and design 

- Design new capability so it connects safely to the existing platform: APIs, events, data and identity

- Select tools and technologies, and define the patterns and practices for AI-native development at Awin

- Weigh long-term maintainability, economic viability and reuse against speed, and document the trade-offs

Spread what works 

- Turn proven builds into reusable patterns, templates and internal tools, and share them so other teams can adopt them without hand-holding

Ways of working 

- Works autonomously, guided by the VP Technology's priorities rather than team-level delivery processes

- Engages directly with engineering, product, data, security and commercial stakeholders as each build requires

Skills & Expertise 

AI-native engineering 

- Builds with coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) as the default way of working. Can show how they decompose work, manage context and review agent output to get production-quality code at pace

- Has shipped LLM-powered features to production: prompt and context engineering, tool use and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval (RAG) and multi-step agent workflows

- Builds evaluations first: test sets, automated evals and regression checks for non-deterministic behaviour, with quality measured before and after release

- Connects models to enterprise systems and data safely, e.g. MCP servers, internal APIs and event streams, with clear permissions and audit trails

- Understands model selection, token economics, latency, caching and fallback strategies, and can explain cost and benefit trade-offs to commercial stakeholders

- Designs for AI-specific security and privacy risks: prompt injection, data leakage, PII handling under GDPR, and guardrails on what models can do

Engineering foundations 

- Expert in at least one modern language (Python or TypeScript ideal), and able to work in our existing Java, PHP and JavaScript estate when integrating

- Strong cloud-native and serverless architecture on AWS, with infrastructure as code (Terraform)

- Experience with event-driven and distributed systems (Kafka/MSK, SQS/SNS) and with relational and non-relational data stores

- Builds observability into everything: tracing, logging and monitoring, including LLM-specific telemetry

- Treats automated testing, CI/CD and secure-by-default design as standard, and automates as much of the delivery loop as possible

Ways of building 

- Takes an idea to a working prototype in days, then hardens it for production, and knows when to stop

- Leaves behind reusable patterns, templates and internal tools, not one-off solutions

Soft skills 

- Bias to action: ships, measures and iterates rather than waiting for perfect requirements

- Comfortable with ambiguity: frames vague opportunities into concrete, testable bets

- Commercially minded: connects technical choices to revenue, cost and customer outcomes, and balances effort against value

- Intellectually honest: kills their own ideas when the evidence says so, and says plainly where AI is not the answer

- Clear communicator: explains technical trade-offs to executives, engineers and commercial teams in language each understands, in writing and in person

- Influences without authority: gets teams to adopt new patterns because they work, not because they're mandated

Our Offer 

- 
Flexi-Week : We prioritise your mental health and wellbeing by offering you a four-day Flexi-Week (with one lighter or completely disconnected day per week) at full pay, with no reduction to your annual holiday allowance.

- 
Flexi-office : We offer an international culture and flexibility through our hybrid/remote working scheme which is designed to foster a culture of mutual trust and working flexibility.

- 
Work Expense Contribution & Remote Working Furniture : You will receive a monthly allowance to cover part of your running costs, as well as a furniture package to support you in setting up a comfortable workspace when working from home.

- 
Health and Wellbeing : With our support and access to various initiatives and sports offers, you can focus on your mental and physical wellbeing.

- 
Development : We’ve built our extensive training suite, Awin Academy, to cover a wide range of skills that support your professional and personal growth, with trainings conveniently packaged to help your overall development.

- 
Appreciation : Thank and reward colleagues by sending them a voucher through our peer-to-peer recognition programme.

We are hiring in multiple countries for this role. Additional benefits, including health and wellbeing offerings, will be discussed during the initial interview. 

Established in 2000, Awin is proud of our dynamic, social and inclusive culture.

Like all businesses, we’ve had to adapt and nurture our culture in a virtual environment. Our virtual ‘Life @ Awin’ hub brings our colleagues from across the globe together for various social activities.

Diversity & Inclusion are paramount to us, and we proudly pursue and hire diverse team members. We champion uniqueness and authenticity; this is who we are at our core. Our network of affiliate partnerships are diverse and transparent, as are the employees powering our vision to build the world’s leading open partner ecosystem. We welcome all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. If you need support at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know.

Awin is part of the Axel Springer group. Learn more at axelspringer.com/ en / , and explore the Axel Springer Essentials here: axelspringer.com/en/inside/the-essentials-what-we-have-adapted-and-why 

Apply now to begin the next stage of your career at a progressive company that supports both your professional and personal development.

title: Mobile Engineer
description:

We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role 

We are looking for mobile developers to build BJAK's AI Neobank App across Android and iOS.

This role is for strong mobile builders who can ship clean, reliable and intuitive mobile experiences, whether their main strength is Android, iOS or both.

What You'll Own 

-

- 
Create simple mobile flows for insurance, payments, claims, renewals and financial services.

- 
Work with product, design and backend teams to turn complex journeys into usable mobile products.

- 
Improve app performance, reliability, crash rate and user experience.

- 
Support fast product launches, experiments and iterations across mobile journeys.

- 
Help set high standards for mobile product quality across the app.

What We're Looking For 

- 
3+ years of mobile development experience in Android, iOS or both.

- 
Strong experience with Kotlin and/or Swift.

- 
Experience shipping production apps used by real users.

- 
Strong product sense and attention to mobile UX.

- 
Able to work with APIs, analytics, crash logs and production feedback.

- 
Fast, practical and comfortable owning work with limited handholding.

- 
App links, GitHub, screenshots or examples of shipped work are a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want 

- 
Thinks like a product builder, not just a mobile coder.

- 
Cares about smooth flows, small details and real user behaviour.

- 
Can work across ambiguity and ship without waiting for perfect specs.

- 
Takes production quality personally.

- 
Honest about what they built directly versus what the wider team delivered.

This Role Is Not For 

- 
Developers who only want to build isolated screens.

- 
People who do not care about UX, performance or reliability.

- 
Candidates who cannot explain their own contribution clearly.

- 
People who need heavy guidance for every task.

- 
Engineers who move slowly in a high-growth environment.

Location 

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Ireland . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Ireland. 

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process 

Our process is designed to move fast:

- 
Online assessment or practical task

- 
Role-specific interview

- 
CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

About the role

Delta builds BLP’s core software: the technical foundation that everything else at the company runs on.

Who we're looking for

Modelling logic and correctness by construction is paramount to us. We aim to express what must be true, prevent invalid states, and keep systems pristine even as they grow.

Thus, we’re looking for highly ambitious engineers who can tackle difficult problems and think precisely. You must be able to make assumptions explicit and use formal, structured reasoning to reach a solution, and explain why it is correct. Typically, strong background in mathematics is a key foundation for this kind of work. We also place a high value on thoroughness and perfectionism.

Tooling wise, we rely heavily on type systems & functional programming.

What you'll do

Our work spans four areas, you will usually work on a given project within one of:

- Infrastructure: Build and operate the cloud infrastructure BLP depends on, covering security, observability and CI/CD.

- Backend: Develop a large codebase, tackling performance, concurrency and the challenges of distributed systems.

- ML: Apply the latest AI technology to complex, real-world business problems and turn it into reliable production software.

- Unbound: Build our product extension platform, enabling BLP to automate arbitrary customer business processes as we scale.

What you'll bring

We do not require experience with any particular technology or even industry software development experience.

You should, however, provide clear evidence of the abilities we’re looking for. That evidence could include:

- strong academic backgrounds (math PhD/MSc or significant olympiad achievements)

- startup experience (early employee, built productive systems yourself & know what it takes to maintain them)

- FP experience (have deep understanding of programming languages and are able to discern the various tradeoffs of different paradigms)

Flexibility. Work on-site in Zurich or remotely within Europe.

title: Senior SW Engineer – Embedded Linux SDK & Distribution (M/W/D)
description:
Mobileye is looking for a passionate Systems Software Developer to join the Operating System Team in the EyeQ Platform Software Group. While many work on Linux, we work in Linux. Our team is responsible for the core OS DNA of the EyeQ computer vision SoC, defining how the system starts, is composed, and manages its lifecycle in a high-performance automotive environment.

We are looking for an experienced systems engineer to join our Core Distribution team . The center of this role is the Linux userspace and the distribution itself: boot and service bring-up, root filesystem composition, and the integration of external SDK into that platform. You will also build Python-based deployment tooling so the OS and SDK stack can be provisioned reproducibly - infrastructure and tool development in service of the OS. 

What will your job look like: 

- Architect and develop Linux userspace and service bring-up so the distribution boots into a consistent, operational platform under embedded constraints. 

- Enable and integrate an SDK into the OS image - drivers, libraries, runtimes, and filesystem layout as first-class distribution components.

- Own distribution composition, including packages, sysroots, and image features that make the SDK and core OS a maintainable, versioned platform.

- Develop Python-based deployment tooling to provision targets with a reproducible OS + SDK environment (image delivery, flashing, and environment setup).

- Debug at the OS boundary - init/service failures, library and ABI mismatches, missing dependencies, and SDK/runtime issues on the target.

- Perform root cause analysis on system-level failures in the distribution, from boot and userspace bring-up through a fully operational stack.

- Collaborate on board bring-up, tailoring the distribution and SDK integration to new EyeQ generations and related target hardware.

All you need is: 

- Outstanding graduate in Computer Science or similar field. 

- 5+ years of experience in Embedded Linux development, with a focus on systems software, userspace, or distribution work.

- Strong C/C++ skills and a solid understanding of POSIX APIs, libraries, and how userspace talks to the kernel.

- Deep knowledge of Linux Internals, specifically the boot process (Bootloaders, Kernel hand-off, Init systems) and root filesystem layout.

- Hands-on experience with Embedded Linux Distributions (e.g., custom Yocto recipes, Buildroot, or Linux-from-scratch).

- Experience enabling vendor SDKs or BSP stacks on Linux — integrating third-party drivers, runtimes, and userspace components into a custom image.

- Proficiency in debugging tools like GDB, Valgrind, strace, and perf.

- Experience with Python for infrastructure and tool development — deployment, packaging, and environment setup.

Nice to have: 

- Background in Automotive Software.

- Experience with GPU/accelerator compute stacks (driver + userspace runtime, inference/compute libraries, cross-sysroot workflows).

- Familiarity with reading hardware schematics and reasoning about basic hardware interfaces and signal.

Mobileye changes the way we drive, from preventing accidents to semi and fully autonomous vehicles. If you are an excellent, bright, hands-on person with a passion to make a difference come to lead the revolution!

title: Senior AI Engineer (GTM)
description:
What do we do? 

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better. 

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally. 

The role: 

We’re looking for an entrepreneurial and technically strong Senior AI Engineer to join our Data & AI team and work with our Go-To-Market organisation.

This is a builder's role, end to end. You’ll work closely with Marketing, Sales, and RevOps to solve high-value problems, design practical AI solutions and build them into reliable systems that people use every day. You’ll be expected to move comfortably from an ambiguous business challenge to a technical design, a working prototype, and then a production-ready solution.

Your work could include building systems that segment and prioritise accounts, developing agents that automate sales workflows, or creating intelligent tools that help our teams research prospects and act on buying signals. You’ll own the full lifecycle of what you build, including evaluation, observability, reliability and cost optimisation.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys being close to users, can write production-quality code and is excited by the challenge of turning rapidly evolving AI capabilities into valuable commercial outcomes. Experience working with GTM teams is useful, but the ability to understand problems, build effective systems and measure their impact is more important.

What you'll do: 

- 
Design and build AI-powered systems for account segmentation, enrichment, scoring, prioritisation and buying-signal detection

- 
Develop and deploy agentic workflows for use cases such as account research, outbound personalisation, call summarisation and CRM hygiene

- 
Write production-quality code and build the integrations, data pipelines and services required to take solutions from prototype to reliable daily use

- 
Optimise systems for quality, latency and cost through evaluation, prompt design, model selection, routing, caching, context management and token optimisation

- 
Establish practical patterns for building AI systems at Paddle, including monitoring, guardrails, documentation and clear measures of business impact

We'd love to hear from you if you: 

- 
Have strong software engineering experience and can independently take a problem from technical design through to production; Python and SQL experience would be particularly relevant

- 
Have hands-on experience building applications with large language models, APIs, retrieval systems, agents or other applied AI technologies

- 
Understand how to evaluate and operate AI systems in production, including managing hallucination risk, latency, reliability, context limits and variable model costs

- 
Are comfortable working with structured and unstructured data, building integrations and turning information from multiple sources into useful systems

- 
Have an interest in commercial problems and can understand concepts such as ICP, segmentation, pipeline, buyer intent and sales workflows; direct GTM experience is beneficial but not essential

- 
Enjoy working directly with the people who use what you build, are comfortable with ambiguity and can balance speed, quality, and long-term maintainability

Everyone is welcome at Paddle 

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We recognise and celebrate that every Paddler is unique and we welcome every individual perspective. As an inclusive employer, we don’t care if, or where, you studied, what you look like or where you’re from. We’re more interested in your craft, curiosity, passion for learning and what you’ll add to our culture. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t match every part of the job ad, especially if you’re part of an underrepresented group.

Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to better support you through the application process and in the workplace. We will do everything we can to support any accommodations needed. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.

Why you’ll love working at Paddle 

We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

- 
Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us” 

- 
Paddle Simply - “Simple can be harder than complex: you have to get your thinking clean to make it simple” 

- 
Paddle for others - “We can realise our wildest dreams, so long as we help enough other people to realise theirs” 

We offer a full suite of benefits, including attractive salaries, stock options, unlimited holidays, enhanced parental leave, retirement plans, private healthcare and well-being initiatives.

We invest in learning and will help you with your personal development via constant exposure to new challenges, an annual learning fund, and regular internal and external training.

Connecting at Paddle 

We’re a ‘digital-first’ company , which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

We recognize that where our Paddlers do their best work is unique to them and we provide trust and autonomy for everyone to work in a way which fits them best. We also value the power of connection and have invested in global hubs which help local communities flourish and bring us together for focused collaboration.

Our Paddle hubs:

- 
In Europe: UK (London headquarters), Portugal (Lisbon hub), Netherlands and Ireland (Dublin hub)

- 
In North America: Austin, TX (USA) and Toronto (Canada)

- 
In APAC : Singapore

Our hub philosophy creates an engaging experience for all Paddlers, wherever, whenever and however we choose to work.

To support this, we focus hiring within our hubs and will always openly share the available locations for each open position on our job description.

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:
Headquarters: New Jersey, USA

URL: https://vertican.com 

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

How we work and what we offer

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

What we offer:

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

- Monthly payments in USD

Vertican is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

title: Data Scientist, Trust & Safety
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

You’ll join the Detection subdomain within Trust & Safety, whose mission is to protect the Vinted community by identifying harmful content and activities. We build detection capabilities that enable timely prevention and moderation, reducing members’ exposure to harm, while minimising disruption to legitimate members.

You’ll develop and improve machine learning models that identify harmful listings and suspicious behaviour across the marketplace, while minimising friction on legitimate members. Working with text, images and behavioural data, you’ll apply practical machine learning techniques to evolving detection challenges.

You’ll work closely with Data Scientists, Decision Scientists, Product Managers and engineers to turn ideas into reliable production solutions. You’ll take ownership of well-defined projects across the ML lifecycle, from understanding the data and developing models to deployment, evaluation and ongoing maintenance.

In this position, you’ll 

- Develop, evaluate and improve machine learning models that detect harmful content and behaviour at scale.

- Engineer features, prepare training and evaluation datasets, understanding their limitations and addressing issues such as noisy labels, class imbalance and data leakage.

- Collaborate with engineers to integrate models into production and develop reliable training and inference pipelines using established tooling.

- Work with Decision Scientists and Product Managers to define success metrics and evaluate model improvements through offline analysis and online experimentation, balancing detection coverage with false positives and member experience.

- Monitor deployed models, investigate changes in their effectiveness and improve them as harmful behaviour and underlying data evolve.

- Write reliable, maintainable and reproducible code, document your work, share learnings and contribute ideas to the team’s roadmap.

About you 

- Practical experience developing machine learning solutions, with a solid foundation in machine learning, statistics and probability theory.

- Proficiency in Python and SQL, and experience with ML libraries such as scikit-learn or PyTorch.

- Hands-on experience preparing training datasets, engineering features, training models and evaluating them against baselines and metrics.

- Experience applying machine learning to at least one of the following: tabular or behavioural data, natural language processing, or computer vision.

- Familiarity with the production ML lifecycle, including deployment, monitoring and retraining.

- Ability to break down problems into manageable steps, work independently within an agreed scope and seek input when needed.

- Ability to communicate your approach, findings and trade-offs clearly, collaborate with technical and non-technical colleagues, and learn from feedback.

- Motivation to apply machine learning to member safety, with care for data privacy and the consequences of incorrect predictions.

Nice to have 

- Experience with fraud detection, content classification or other Trust & Safety applications.

- Experience with transformers, multimodal models or LLM-based workflows.

Work perks

- 25 days of paid annual leave

title: Cloud Architect
description:
About Vitestro 

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™) . This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement. 

We are looking for a Cloud Architect to shape and implement Vitestro's cloud platform with a clear, pragmatic technical direction. Our infrastructure runs on AWS and supports mission-critical, regulated medical device software. Vitestro is also realizing its first integration with Laboratory Information System (LIS) over the cloud, and delivering that connection is a core part of this role. We need someone who translates real operational and business constraints into working systems — someone whose first instinct is "what does this actually need to do, reliably and affordably," not "what's the most sophisticated way to solve this."

You will join the Platform & Connectivity team and build alongside its cloud, backend, and DevOps engineers. This is an individual-contributor technical leadership role, not a people-management position — you carry the architectural vision and build it hands-on with the team, rather than designing something for others to execute.

If you'd rather ship a solid, working solution than iterate endlessly toward a theoretically ideal one, and you have a track record of keeping cloud costs under control at scale, you'll thrive in this role.

First months at Vitestro 

In your first months, you get to know our cloud platform, the device connectivity and the team. You review the current architecture, its costs and its production-readiness, and identify where the biggest risks and quick wins are. You take ownership of the cloud architecture for our first LIS integration, and you agree with the team on the first architectural standards for observability, logging and infrastructure as code.

This is what success looks like: 

After 12 months, our first LIS integration runs reliably in production, with monitoring, alerting and failure handling in place. Cloud costs are predictable and under control, and key architectural decisions and trade-offs are recorded. The team uses shared patterns instead of reinventing solutions, and is confident running production systems as we move from pre-market to post-market.

Key Responsibilities: 

- Set the technical direction for our AWS-based cloud platform and build it hands-on with the team — weighing cost, operability, and production-readiness as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts

- Own the cloud architecture of Vitestro's first LIS integration over the cloud: secure, reliable, and traceable data exchange between our platform and the hospital laboratory

- Choose solutions on their merits rather than defaulting to the most AWS-native option — including other clouds, self-hosted tooling, or dedicated infrastructure when that's genuinely the better fit

- Take implementations from a working prototype to something that's production-ready — monitoring, alerting, and failure handling included. You bring experience with production systems and advise the team on how to navigate from pre-market to post-market stages.

- Establish architectural standards and patterns so similar problems (e.g. observability, logging, data pipelines) get solved consistently instead of reinvented each time

- Keep cloud costs in check as part of everyday engineering decisions, catching expensive mistakes before they show up on an invoice

- Balance short-term solutions driven by business needs and deadlines against the long-term architecture: make each trade-off explicit, record it, and plan the path from the tactical fix to the durable solution

- Diagnose and resolve production issues across the cloud platform from logs, metrics, and traces

What You’ll Bring: 

- Deep, hands-on production experience with AWS at scale — not certification-level familiarity, but real experience with what breaks and what gets expensive as usage grows

- Proven experience running production systems end to end, from design and release through monitoring and incident response, and the ability to advise a team that is new to production

- Genuine experience building outside an AWS-only mindset — another cloud, self-hosted/open-source alternatives, or dedicated/on-premise infrastructure — enough to make an informed trade-off, not just AWS as the only tool you reach for

- A track record of finishing what others started: turning a partial or unstable implementation into something genuinely reliable in production

- Strong Infrastructure as Code practice (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, or AWS CDK) as the authoritative source of environment configuration

- Comfortable operating in a regulated, security-conscious environment where architecture decisions have compliance implications

- Familiarity with AWS cost structure, along with the ability to factor in cost-related considerations when designing infrastructure

- Professional English; Dutch is a plus

Nice to have: 

- Experience specifically with observability/logging platforms at scale (e.g. OpenSearch, Grafana/Loki stacks, or equivalent) — bringing an implementation to production-hardened state, not just standing it up

- Experience in medical device, healthcare, or another regulated industry

- Familiarity with multi-tenant, per-customer cloud architectures (e.g. isolated accounts or workloads per client/region)

- Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

How We Work 

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

- We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

- We focus on execution and delivering results.

- We proactively remove blockers and help each other succeed.

- We challenge ideas, not people.

- We continuously learn, improve, and raise the bar.

- We celebrate team success over individual heroics.

We move fast, but we do so thoughtfully. We care deeply about quality because the technology we build ultimately impacts patients and healthcare professionals.

If you are looking for an environment where you can make a significant contribution, take ownership of meaningful work, and be surrounded by highly motivated colleagues, we'd love to meet you.

What we offer 

- Competitive salary including a pension plan

- 25 days of annual leave (full-time position)

- A high-skilled team based in Utrecht

- Frequent out-of-work team activities and an annual company weekend away

- A training budget

- The chance to help shape the new niche of autonomous medical robotics

We’re big fans of working from the office – this is where team spirit comes alive. At the same time, we offer flexibility, allowing up to two (out of 5) days of working from home for those who prefer it. 

Are you excited? 

We totally understand that and so are we! By joining us, you can play an active role in changing the future of health care. Excited to join our revolution? Then we’d love to hear from you! 

If you think you've got what it takes, but you don't meet all the requirements - we still recommend you apply. We would love to learn about your interest and experience and consider if you can be a good fit for Vitestro. Nobody is a perfect fit, and we welcome applications with imperfections. We offer a learning environment where we grow together!

title: Lead AI Engineer, LLM Systems
description:
Company Overview 

hermeneutic research is a best-in-class proprietary trading firm. It deploys research-driven discretionary and systematic strategies as well as makes strategic long-term investments. The partners' decade-long history of success in trading and business building and a firm-wide cultural emphasis on alpha generation, open debate, relentless iteration, and teamwork are key to the firm's continued expansion in a challenging market environment that has hamstrung competitors. A hard-wired emphasis on risk management and opportunistic market participation ensures that hermeneutic research will continue its growth trajectory in the coming decades.

Job Overview 

You will own a multi-agent research system as production infrastructure: make it faster, cheaper, measurably better and efficient.

hermeneutic Research Labs is the firm’s applied research and engineering unit. Its first product is a research intelligence platform for both traditional and digital-asset markets, built with our researchers and traders and used by them every day. The platform turns market, on-chain, macro and news data into event-driven research that trading decisions rely on. The platform is held to the standard we apply to our own trading: rigorous, falsifiable and measured on outcomes.

The Labs is making a multi-year investment to turn the platform into production infrastructure that a growing set of internal users can depend on. As part of that investment, it is hiring a Lead AI Engineer.

The LLM layer is yours for years. A research query runs through multiple agent stages across several model providers and our own self-hosted models. You start with your hands on the system, writing code and running experiments. As the function grows, you will hire and lead its engineers. The role is built to grow into Head of AI Engineering.

Key Responsibilities

- Keep the LLM layer reliable: latency budgets, concurrency and queueing, declared degradation modes, structured-output validation and provider failover.

- Build evaluation tied to research outcomes: offline sets from real queries with outcome labels, online experiments, regression gates on every change, and model-generated confidence calibrated with quantitative research before it reaches a decision.

- Control cost and routing: per-workload cost attribution, difficulty-based routing between small and frontier models, caching and batching, and the economics of self-hosted serving and GPU capacity.

- Run model strategy and lifecycle: pinned model versions, replayable test batteries before any change, one-step rollback, provider diversification, and fine-tuning or adapters where they pay.

- Shape the agent architecture with evidence: ablate and retire components that do not earn their keep, and improve tool use, memory and retrieval only where they move research outcomes.

- Ground and trace outputs: citation, hallucination controls, audit trails, and the boundary between what a model may assert and what it may only suggest.

- Build the team: review and mentor engineers now, and hire and lead an AI engineering group as the function grows.

Requirements

Must-Haves 

- 7+ years of software or ML engineering, including 3+ years shipping LLM-backed systems to real users in production, where you owned latency, cost and quality, and 2+ years leading other engineers while still shipping.

- A track record of building a function from nothing.

- Command of inference economics: tokens, caching, routing, structured outputs, tool use and quantisation, with cost-per-request figures for the systems you ran.

- Measurement discipline: you instrument before changing anything, evaluate against outcomes rather than model judges, have built an eval that caught what a vibe check missed, and have retired a component with data.

- Strong Python, including async concurrency.

- Experience with self-hosted serving (vLLM or similar), adapters and GPU capacity planning, or an end-to-end provider migration.

- Depth in vector and graph retrieval, built and measured, with an informed view on when retrieval is the wrong fix.

Technologies named here are what we run today, not a filter. We hire for depth and judgement.

Desired Attributes

- Directness: you tell the author when their component does not earn its keep.

- Sound judgement working alongside AI coding agents on a largely AI-written codebase, keeping ownership of what ships.

- Initiative: you take on the hard, unowned problem first, and bring the profiling data and a first fix.

- Bonus: fine-tuning and preference optimisation in production, and an informed view on when multi-agent frameworks are over-built.

- Bonus: finance or trading exposure, and experience hiring engineers.

Interview Process 

- 
CV Screening – We will review your application based on the qualifications and experience outlined above.

- 
Hiring Manager Screen – A conversation about the LLM systems you have run in production.

- 
Systems Deep-Dive – A whiteboard session on LLM systems design.

- 
Hands-On Round – A take-home on a synthetic trace set with a review, or a live debugging session.

- 
Reliability and Measurement Scenarios – A scenario discussion with peers from research or risk.

- 
Collaboration and AI-Assisted Work – A conversation on how you work with teammates and AI coding agents.

- 
Co-Founder Interview – A concluding discussion to assess your capabilities, strategic thinking, and cultural fit.

Company Values 

Throughout the process, you'll be assessed for cultural fit through our company values:

- 
Drive – We believe the best team members are deeply passionate about what they do. That passion fuels their growth, drives them to seek out the best teams, and leads them to hold high expectations of themselves in pursuit of excellence.

- 
Ownership – We aim to extend ownership as broadly as possible across the firm. In return, we value people who take initiative, step up when needed, and treat the company’s goals as their own.

- 
Judgment – We value those who see the big picture and focus on what truly drives impact and results. They use time wisely, adapt across domains, and always prioritize outcomes over comfort zones.

- 
Openness – We foster a culture of open communication, mutual challenge, and shared growth. We believe constructive debate and proactive knowledge sharing lead us closer to the truth—and better decisions.

- 
Competence – We work with people who bring exceptional intellectual strength. What sets them apart isn’t just what they know—it’s how they use what they know to navigate change, adapt quickly, and contribute meaningfully in fast-changing environments.

- 
Resilience – We perform under pressure. Markets move fast, and so do we—but we stay grounded, focused, and calm. We embrace uncertainty, learn from setbacks, and adapt quickly without losing sight of long-term goals.

title: Senior Applied Scientist, Efficient LLM Inference & Model Optimization
description:
About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. You will own focused research and optimization projects, write strong code, and produce prototypes, publications, and technical artifacts that engineers can build on.

Your research will span quantization, distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, and model/runtime co-optimization, alongside inference engines and distributed inference architectures. You will investigate how these approaches interact, evaluate their trade-offs across model quality, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and cost per token, and work with engineering teams to bring promising results into production.

Your responsibilities

- Lead research projects in efficient LLM and VLM inference, from hypotheses and experiments through ablations, prototypes, and production handoff.

- Develop and evaluate methods spanning quantization, quantization-aware training (QAT), distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, KV-cache compression, long-context inference, MoE routing, and model/runtime co-optimization.

- Build prototypes using PyTorch, Triton, CUDA-adjacent tooling, or inference-serving frameworks, and collaborate with MLEs and platform engineers to turn them into production components.

- Research LLM request routing and scheduling strategies, including cache-aware load balancing and prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD). Evaluate how queueing, KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and prefill/decode capacity allocation affect latency, throughput, and serving cost.

- Investigate multi-node inference for dense and mixture-of-experts models, including wide expert parallelism (WideEP). Study expert placement, load imbalance, and computation/communication trade-offs, and use the findings to guide model and system architecture choices.

- Develop rigorous evaluations covering quality, latency, throughput, numerical stability, memory footprint, tail latency, and cost per token. Compare serving architectures under consistent workload conditions and GPU budgets.

- Work with MLE, GPU kernel, backend infrastructure, product, and customer teams to select research priorities with measurable production impact.

- Share results through internal reports, technical blogs, papers, and open-source artifacts, and mentor engineers and scientists on experimental design, scientific rigor, and model/system trade-offs.

Must-haves

- A PhD in computer science, machine learning, ML systems, computer systems, computer architecture, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, or a closely related discipline.

- A strong publication record or equivalent research artifacts in ML, ML systems, efficient inference, model compression, quantization, distillation, serving systems, or related areas.

- Strong Python and PyTorch implementation skills, with the ability to turn ideas into experiments and working prototypes.

- Deep knowledge of LLMs, VLMs, transformer inference, decoding algorithms, model compression, quantization, and production-serving trade-offs.

- Strong experimental design skills covering ablations, baselines, metrics, statistical reasoning, and failure analysis.

- Excellent written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-haves

- First-author publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP, ASPLOS, OSDI, SOSP, ISCA, or HPCA.

- Experience deploying ML models or inference optimizations in production.

- Experience with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, CUDA, or PyTorch internals.
